stories.title: A U.S. cruise ship suspends a global voyage due to fuel costs, stranding 200 passengers
bullet_points: A U.S.
cruise ship on an around-the-world voyage that touted its cabins as floating homes suspended its three-year journey in Cambodia due to fuel costs, forcing hundreds of passengers to disembark.

stories.title: Flávio Bolsonaro calls himself the ‘leader of Brazil’ after fleeing to Miami
bullet_points: Far-right senator and family land in US after crossing from Brazil into Argentina and then flying via Ecuador   Flávio Bolsonaro  declared himself the “true president” of  Brazil  after losing last Sunday’s presidential election and fleeing to the United States.

After landing on a private jet with his family in Miami,  Florida , on Wednesday morning, the far-right senator published the claim in a letter – even though his own party has recognised the legitimate victory of  Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva , as have all of Brazil’s institutions, and international observers who monitored and endorsed the vote.

stories.title: EU backs away from offer to Canada to start ‘associate member’ talks
bullet_points: Watered-down version of statement to be issued at end of Montreal summit instead offers ‘ever closer association’  The EU has backed away from its offer to Canada to start talks on becoming an “associate member” after disagreements between member states just as an EU-Canada summit was set to begin in Montreal.

A draft of a joint statement to be issued after the end of the summit, which runs Thursday and Friday, showed a watered-down version offering “an ever closer association of Canada to the EU, short of full membership itself”.
Continue reading...

stories.title: US ambassador suggests Trump could blame Canada if midterms don’t go his way
bullet_points: Pete Hoekstra, controversial US ambassador to Canada, has also accused Canadian officials of interfering in US elections  The US ambassador has suggested Canada could be blamed if Republicans perform poorly in next week’s midterm elections, the latest intervention from a controversial figure who has been accused of inflaming a bitter dispute that has angered and baffled residents of both countries.

On Wednesday, CTV news  reported  that Pete Hoekstra told business leaders at a closed door meeting that if a number of swing races – including Maine and Michigan – go to the Democrats, it could make things harder for Canada because Donald Trump might try to blame the loss on it.
Continue reading...

stories.title: Egypt fines prominent editor Lina Attalah and shuts independent news outlet Mada Masr
bullet_points: Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website  Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country.
Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt.

stories.title: A US woman feared dead was reported alive in Mexico. But police now say that isn’t true
bullet_points: Mexican police had said they found Shayna Feinman in Tijuana, raising the hopes of missing Arizonan’s family   Arizona  authorities say their  Mexican  counterparts were resoundingly mistaken when they publicly claimed recently that they found alive a woman who was feared slain after disappearing in 2024 – a turn of events that her sister has called “turmoil” and “heartbreaking”.
The case in question centers on Shayna Feinman, who was reported missing in rural Yavapai county, Arizona, in March 2024 at age 38.

stories.title: Africa’s ‘unprecedented’ Ebola outbreak could reach UK, says top health official
bullet_points: Jean Kaseya, of the Africa CDC, warns of the illness spreading like Covid unless more funding is secured to increase preparedness and possible treatment  The “unprecedented”  spread of the Ebola outbreak  means it could reach the UK and other countries, according to one of Africa’s top health officials.

As the current outbreak reached  10,000 cases, with almost 5,000 deaths , Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), compared the outbreak to the Covid pandemic, which first took hold in China before spreading to countries across the world, claiming millions of lives, and ravaging health systems and economies.
